questions.answer: Crustdata prices in credits, and it still publishes no plan grid or dollar price per credit. Per-endpoint rates are 0.03 credits per search result, 1–7 per person enrich and 2–4 per company enrich. Its own cost post puts the lowest tier at $95 a month, with the credit's dollar value set by plan. Each plan grants recurring monthly credits, which are spent first. Purchased top-ups roll over and expire 12 months after purchase, and auto top-up is available. The reseller treg.to charges $0.009 per search result and $2.10 per person enrich at what it calls Crustdata's own rate, which implies about $0.30 per credit (inference).

claims.claim: Crustdata's cost guide gives per-endpoint credits (search 0.03 per result, person enrich 1–7, company enrich 2–4), says the dollar value per credit is set by plan, and puts the lowest tier at $95/month.
Crustdata's pricing page shows no plan prices and no per-credit dollar rate. It describes credit-based usage tiers with monthly or annual billing and sends enterprise pricing to sales.

Crustdata balances sit in two wallets. The recurring wallet holds the plan's per-cycle credit grant and is spent first. The top-up wallet holds purchased credits, which roll over month to month and expire 12 months after each purchase. Automatic top-ups are supported.
The reseller treg.to sells Crustdata people and company search at $0.009 per result and person enrich at $2.10 per result, and says it passes through the provider's own rate with no markup.

questions.notes: r5 (crustdata.co/pricing) redirects to r10; the page HTML contains no prices. The $0.30 per credit figure is my inference from treg.to (0.03 × $0.30 = $0.009 and 7 × $0.30 = $2.10); treg.to says the rate is not Crustdata's subscription pricing. r17's free tier of 100 credits a month is only 'commonly cited' and may come from Salesmotion's own free tier (r15), so I did not count it. r9 and r4 say credits expire after 6 months, while the docs (r7, r23) say 12. The KB already flags this conflict. r19 says new accounts get free credits with no card. r21 and r12 give only estimates or quote-based labels.

questions.answer: No. There is no company or entity type: the Search API's search_type is web, fast or people. Perplexity's official Node SDK also exposes a search_mode of web, academic or sec on search.create, for scholarly sources and SEC filings. The public API reference omits search_mode, and the KB calls those modes Sonar-only. Structured financial data for public companies is only in the Agent API's finance_search tool.

claims.claim: Perplexity's Search API reference allows search_type web, fast or people only, with no company or entity type.

Perplexity's official Node SDK types the Search API request with search_mode 'web', 'academic' or 'sec' (SEC mode targets filings, not company entities), and its README shows an academic search through client.search.create.
Structured financial data for public companies and ETFs comes from the Agent API's finance_search tool, billed at $5 per 1,000 invocations.

questions.notes: I checked C2 against Perplexity's own repo (perplexityai/perplexity-node). In src/generated/api.ts, synced 2026-09-25, ApiSearchRequestInput has search_mode set to web, academic or sec alongside search_type set to web, fast or people. The README's Academic Search example calls client.search.create. Perplexity's docs show search_mode only under Sonar, and the public Search API reference omits it. KB lines 93 and 269 say academic and SEC were Sonar-only and that the Search API has no paper category; line 269 tells readers not to repeat Exa's 'Academic/SEC modes' claim. Whether the server honours search_mode on /search was not tested. r24 (Perplexity blog) returned 403. r1 (Exa /versus) still says Perplexity has no people or company search; the KB already marks the people part false.

questions.answer: Brave publishes no exact API query count, only round and inconsistent figures. Its 2026-02-24 post claims billions of API calls a week. Its ads chief JP Schmetz told MediaPost (2026-04-06) that the API gets several billion queries a month, and he declined to give exact numbers. Its 2026-04-01 post says the index handles over 2 billion queries a month across the API and end-user search combined.

claims.claim: Brave's 2026-02-24 post says Search API usage has grown exponentially, with thousands of new sign-ups a day and billions of API calls a week.
JP Schmetz, Brave Search's chief of ads, told MediaPost (2026-04-06) that the API receives several billion queries a month but declined to share exact numbers.
Brave's 2026-04-01 post says its 40-billion-page index handles over 2 billion monthly queries across the API and end-user search combined.

questions.notes: Billions of calls a week implies roughly 9B or more a month. That is at or above several billion a month, and well above the 2B+ a month Brave gives for the API and end-user search combined. The KB should present these as inconsistent vendor claims. Other volume figures in the pool describe Brave Search as a whole, not the API: 1.6B a month (r12), 16B a year (AWS listing, r4/r22), tens of millions a day (API help docs, r21), and 50M consumer searches a day (r6). MediaPost also quotes Schmetz naming Snowflake, Cohere and Mistral as major API customers. r14 (dev.to) cites 35,000 free and 2,700 paid API customers as of March 2025 (secondary; not counted).

questions.answer: The live Websets billing page returns 429, so I read its Wayback capture of 2026-05-09; a review dated 2026-09-07 matches it. Plans: Starter is $49/mo for 8,000 credits, with 100 results per Webset, 2 seats, 10 enrichments and 2 concurrent searches. Pro is $449/mo for 100,000 credits, with 1,000 results, 10 seats, 50 enrichments and 5 concurrent searches. Enterprise is custom (5,000 results, 100 enrichments, volume discounts). claims.claim: The $49/month Websets plan (8,000 credits a month) is named Starter and includes 100 results per Webset, 2 team seats and 10 enrichments per Webset.

Pro costs $449/month for 100,000 credits, with 1,000 results per Webset, 10 seats and 50 enrichments. Enterprise is custom, with 5,000 results and 100 enrichments per Webset and volume credit discounts.

Websets credit costs: 10 per result matching all criteria, 0 for non-matches, 5 per email or phone number, 2 per row for other enrichments, 2 per resolved import result, 2 per API preview request and 5 per API recall estimate.
The Free plan gives 1,000 credits and caps a Webset at 25 verified results.

questions.answer: Pricing is not published. The Batch API is an Enterprise-only beta (header batches-2026-06-06) that Exa enables through sales. No price, discount, item cap, SLA or retention period appears in the docs or pricing pages. Documented limits: POST items to /search or /agent/runs only, each with a batch-unique customId of 1–64 characters. Results come back as a JSONL file through a short-lived presigned URL. List pages default to 100 items, with no upper bound.

claims.claim: The Batch API is a beta (Exa-Beta header batches-2026-06-06) available only to Enterprise teams after Exa enables it through sales.
Batch items must be POST requests to /search or /agent/runs with a batch-unique customId; results come back as a JSONL file through a short-lived presigned URL.
Exa's pricing page and pricing docs list no Batch API price or discount.
